Web search 2026-11-20 (wyofile.com, damindex.com, fs.usda.gov project 57080): New Fork Lake is held by a 1925 irrigation dam (37 ft high) - a regulated reservoir, so the sand band is measured to its landward edge

Esri World Imagery 2026-11-20 (600 m export frame; z19 tiles north and east of the loop): the loop sits in burned forest (standing snags, open ground, no canopy); a 25-35 m bare sand band rings the lake; the pad north of the loop road at ~43.0838,-109.9655 (site 8 on the FS map) is ~35-40 m from the landward edge of the sand over open burned ground; site 10's pad (~43.0838,-109.9663) ~45 m; the east side of the loop is 65 m+ from the sand

note: Bridger-Teton NF primitive campground on the south shore of New Fork Lake, a dam-raised lake about 24 miles from Pinedale; the unpaved access road is passable by passenger car. Sites in a burned-over forest; sites 8 and 10 on the north side of the loop are nearest the water, the rest well back. A sandy day-use beach adjoins. Food storage required; no trash service. --Claude
summary: FS page + 2017 FS site map + rec.gov 10289165 read: 15 sites (16 -> 15), pullouts 35-53 ft (site 1 90 ft), no water or hookups, vault toilet, FCFS scan-and-pay, 14-day limit, $12. Lakefront kept with a caveat naming sites 8 and 10 (~35-45 m to the high-water edge over open burned ground). Phone empty -> 307-367-4326. Pin fine.
flags: WATERFRONT (checked hard): lakefront kept, borderline. New Fork Lake is dam-raised (1925 irrigation dam), so measured to the landward edge of the 25-35 m sand band. Sites 8 (pad ~43.0838,-109.9655) and 10 (~43.0838,-109.9663) on the loop's north side - FS map numbering - are ~35-45 m from it over open burned ground (standing snags, no canopy); the other 13 sites are 65 m+ back. All FCFS nightly. The stored waterfront_evidence calls the lake 'natural' and says loops 'meet an open sandy beach apron' - the beach is the separate day-use area. If the curator reads ~45 m through snags as too far, lakeview.
NOTE: 'among aspens' (FS prose) dropped - imagery shows burned conifer; '16 single sites' was wrong (15).
SEASON not written: FS 'Seasons of Use June 1' gives only an opening date; rec.gov's fee season 05-22..11-30 is a rate window, not the open season.
LEAD/NEIGHBOUR: New Fork Lake Group Campground (rec.gov 231913, 43.083056,-109.965556) beside the loop - group-only, not a lead.
